# shape-ops - context for bug hunters

Scope: `jix/src/ops/shape_ops/*.rs` (non-test parts). Bare file names (`slice.rs:121`) are in
`jix/src/ops/shape_ops/`; other paths are relative to `jix/src/` unless they start with `jix-py/`.
`mod.rs` is now only `mod`/`pub use` lines; each op's `Array::<op>()` wrapper (which `unwrap()`s,
documented panics) moved to the bottom of the op's own file (#97/#98).

Facts that change how to read this code:
- Release builds have overflow checks OFF (no profile override in jix/Cargo.toml): unchecked `+`/`*`
  wrap in shipped wheels and panic in debug/tests.
- x86 and armv7 (32-bit) wheels ship but are never tested. Since #103 a request's sizes are `usize`
  and `check_region_size` (error.rs:298-312, 32-bit only) caps region bytes at isize::MAX, so most
  per-op `as usize` casts are bounded by the region; DIMS (u64, up to i64::MAX) are not.
- `read_data` is effectively crate-internal: `OutBuf` has only `pub(crate)` constructors
  (storage/buf.rs:450-467). The safe surface is `Array::to_buf_strided{,_into}` / `to_ndarray*`
  (array/read.rs:173-471), which validate the ranges and build the `Index`.
- No shape op overrides `read_as_elementwise_pipeline`; the default (storage/core_trait.rs:111-125)
  pulls and wraps the buffer, so a shape op's pull result (incl. 0 strides) feeds pipelines directly.
- Python wrappers (index parsing, `-1`, dim normalization, dtype promotion) live in
  `jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs`; the core ops below never promote.

## Purpose
Lazy views that change shape/order without changing values. Three read strategies:
(1) re-stride forwarders - PermuteDims, InsertDim, RemoveDim (via `read_data_and_map_strides`),
Broadcast pull (0 strides), Slice step-1 (forward) and Slice stepped over a PLAIN_READ inner in pull
mode (box read + stride*step); plus transparent forwards: Flip/Roll identity, Roll non-wrap, Tile
case A, Concatenate inside one member; (2) split-and-forward - Slice stepped (general path), Roll
wrap, Tile case B, Reshape, Concatenate, Stack: several inner push reads into sub-buffers of `out`;
(3) read-then-copy - Flip, Repeat, Tile case C, Broadcast push: pull the inner region, `NdCopier`
into the destination. Each op also derives an `ArraySpecDynamic` (block shape, fixed dims, scale
weights, layout order, cache ids) and, since #100, most own a `CacheScope`.

## Contracts

### Relied on
- `Index` (storage/index.rs:10-19): `start.len() == size.len() <= NDIM_MAX`, every size >= 1, no
  `start + size` overflow. Only `Index::new` (31-35) checks; `new_unchecked` (44-49) is `unsafe` with a
  `debug_assert` only, and `size()` transmutes `NonZeroUsize` (76-77). Callers of `read_data` never
  send an empty region: array/read.rs:232, 386-388, 451-453 return early instead.
- `read_data` modes (core_trait.rs:70-98, buf.rs:449-501): pull = put any buffer covering the region
  at any strides (incl. 0) into the empty slot; push = write the region at `out`'s strides.
  `OutBuf::materialize` (buf.rs:474-488) returns `out` itself in push mode, or allocates
  UNINITIALIZED pool memory (util/buf_pool.rs:35-50, whole capacity exposed 109-120) with strides
  from `strides_for_layout_order(read_layout_order)` (util/mod.rs:164-179) in pull mode.
- `check_out_buf` (buf.rs:351-364): `check_get_range` (error.rs:249-259), `check_region_size`, and for
  push `check_out_buf_impl` (383-431): stride count, writable, strides non-overlapping over the region
  (dims of length 1 ignored), and `out` long enough. Every shape op calls it first, except Flip/Roll
  identity, which delegate to the inner (same shape) that checks. Because every storage checks its own
  `out`, a mis-sized sub-buffer from a split op is an Err in the callee, not UB; a wrong but in-bounds
  offset is a silent wrong result.
- `out` must not overlap memory any input reads (`NdCopier` noalias, util/nd_copy.rs:41-56;
  `from_raw_parts_mut` docs buf.rs:89-97). Not checked anywhere; caller's duty.
- `NdCopier::copy` (util/nd_copy.rs:41-56): both byte ranges cover every touched byte, no overlap,
  same dtype as `new`.
- Shapes of all arrays satisfy `check_shape_overflow` (error.rs:192-205): dims <= i64::MAX and the
  product (zero dims counted as 1, util/mod.rs:224-234) times itemsize fits u64. So region products
  and logical strides fit u64.
- `read_cached` (context.rs:148-243) hits only on exact `(id, start, size)`; a pull result from the
  cache is a read-only `Shared` buffer; push reads are never stored. So cache scopes affect memory
  and speed, never values (read results are pure functions of storage + index).

### Provided
- Every read writes EVERY element of the region (push) or returns a buffer valid for every element
  (pull). `to_ndarray_sub` `assume_init()`s its destination (array/read.rs:243) and pool memory is
  uninitialized, so a skipped element is an uninitialized read (UB for bool8).
- `dtype()`/`ElementType` equal the inner's. Stack/Concatenate: `ArraysT::ElementType`
  (util/arr_sequence.rs:82-85; tuples require one shared ET, 652-658) plus a runtime full-`Dtype`
  equality check (concatenate.rs:104-109, stack.rs:80-85).
- `spec()`: `block_shape.len() == ndim` with entries in `1..=max(dim,1)` (test_util.rs:981-989 allows
  0); `read_layout_order` a permutation of `0..ndim`. Documented as a "pure hint" (params.rs:602-611)
  but `strides_for_layout_order` and `to_ndarray_sub`'s `permuted_axes` (array/read.rs:207-228) index
  with it: a non-permutation panics or yields aliasing pull strides.
- Flags: InsertDim/RemoveDim keep PLAIN_READ, clear IS_COMPACT (insert_dim.rs:203-208,
  remove_dim.rs:201-206). Slice/Flip/Roll in the identity case return the inner's spec unchanged
  (flags, cache ids) and its `as_compact()` (slice.rs:221-239, flip.rs:179-197, roll.rs:159-177);
  every other op clears all flags and `as_compact()` is None. Consumers: `MaybeCompact::new`
  (ops/maybe_compact.rs:32), `write_to` (archive/array.rs:407-416: writes the inner's blocks under the
  OUTER `self.shape()`), Slice's fast path (slice.rs:150), `small_read` (array/read.rs:458).
- Cache ids: each op does `add_cache_ids_from(inner)` then `with_cache_scope()` (params.rs:852-908),
  entering the scope in `read_data`. Exceptions: Broadcast never scopes (broadcast.rs:99); InsertDim
  skips it when all inserted dims are in front (insert_dim.rs:123-127); Concatenate merges with
  `repeats_across_inners = false` (concatenate.rs:155-161), Stack with true (stack.rs:139).
- Construction validation: `check_shape_overflow` in Broadcast (broadcast.rs:61), Repeat (64), Tile
  (80), Reshape (57), Concatenate (120, after `checked_add` 112-117), Stack (96); `check_ndim` in
  InsertDim (63), Stack (93), Reshape (47), SliceSpec::try_from (slice.rs:281); Repeat/Tile require
  `ndim < NDIM_MAX` (repeat.rs:42-47, tile.rs:58-63) for their (ndim+1)-d copy.

### Preconditions of pub(crate) unsafe fns used here
- `read_data_and_map_strides` (buf.rs:517-554), "caller should ensure the created strides are
  valid": the closures are inverse per-dim correspondences, `inner_index` is the same region
  re-indexed, and any dim dropped by outer2inner or given stride 0 by inner2outer has extent 1. Pull
  relabels the CALLER's slot in place with `set_strides` (544); push re-strides `out` and forwards it
  (548-551). Callers: permute_dims.rs:130-139, insert_dim.rs:172-191 (pull: inserted dims stride 0),
  remove_dim.rs:170-189 (push: removed dims stride 0). Established by the constructors.
- `Index::new_unchecked`: every call site in shape_ops (slice.rs:142,162,209; reshape.rs:367;
  permute_dims.rs:133; insert_dim.rs:175; remove_dim.rs:173; broadcast.rs:145; flip.rs:116;
  roll.rs:109,140; tile.rs:150,183,198; repeat.rs:136; concatenate.rs:241,321; stack.rs:219) must
  derive non-zero sizes from the request. See Hot spots for the ones that need reasoning.
- `set_strides` (buf.rs:249-258): writable buffers keep the `from_slice_mut` no-alias contract;
  `make_readonly` first for aliasing strides. `from_slice_mut` (126-140), `copy_from` (261-288).

## Unsafe inventory
- buf.rs:544 - `set_strides` on the inner's pull buffer in the forwarders. Non-aliasing kept because
  0 strides go only to extent-1 dims. Inner may hand back a writable PoolBufMut (materializing ops) or
  a read-only borrow/`Shared`. The old lifetime `transmute` is gone (slot API, #104).
- buf.rs:550 - `from_slice_mut(out data, inner strides)`: permuted/subset strides of a checked `out`.
- slice.rs:170 - `set_strides(stride*step, or itemsize for len<=1)` on the inner's pull of the box.
  Sound for ANY inner (the pull contract covers the box; stepped strides select a subset);
  PLAIN_READ only makes it cheap. Relies on the box `Index` being right (32-bit, see Suspicions).
- broadcast.rs:160-161 - `make_readonly` then 0 strides: pull results with aliasing strides are
  never writable. broadcast.rs:167 - `copy_from(inner pull, 0-stride src)` into checked `out`.
- Sub-buffer `from_slice_mut(&mut out_buf[off..], strides)`: slice.rs:201-206, reshape.rs:361-366,
  roll.rs:133-138, tile.rs:178-183, concatenate.rs:303-316, stack.rs:226-238. Safe slicing (panics if
  `off > len`), callee re-checks extent. Concatenate/Stack fast paths pass an exactly sized packed
  slot (`off..off+bytes`), valid only if `out` is row-major packed AND the dims before the joined dim
  are <= 1.
- `NdCopier::copy` with `get_unchecked(off..)` / `get_unchecked_mut(off..)` (an offset past the end
  is immediate UB, not a panic): flip.rs:155-164, repeat.rs:181-202, tile.rs:217-228, 256-267,
  279-290. src offsets bounded by `idx < out_shape` on the inner's pull buffer; dst offsets by `out`
  passing `check_out_buf` for the full region (local reasoning, all extents <= the u-size region).
- core_trait.rs:124 - default `OperandTyped::new_input(pull buffer)`, inherited by all shape ops.

## Edge-case surface
- Empty requests: impossible since #103 - all the old per-op "empty read" returns were deleted
  (`debug_assert!(!size.contains(&0))` remains). Ops must not CREATE an empty sub-Index:
  Concatenate skips zero-length members (concatenate.rs:272-274); Roll wrap has len1, len2 >= 1
  because `s < shift < e`; Tile B has len1, len2 >= 1; Repeat `g_end - g_start >= 1`.
- Length-0 dims in shapes: no read reaches them. Repeat/Tile with `repeats == 0` or L == 0, and
  Broadcast to a 0 dim, give zero-element arrays. Tile's `s % l` (tile.rs:144) relies on L > 0,
  implied by a non-empty request (the comment at 141-142 still mentions a removed short-circuit).
- 0-d arrays: NdIter over `[]` yields one index (util/iter/nd.rs:584); Reshape `[] <-> [1,1]`,
  InsertDim of 0-d, RemoveDim to 0-d, Stack of 0-d (`[n]`) and Slice with 0 items (`TryFrom(&[])`,
  all-steps-1 forward) go through 0-dim `Index`es. Roll/Repeat/Tile/Concatenate reject ndim 0.
- Length-1 dims: InsertDim pull / RemoveDim push / Reshape unmatched orig dims (reshape.rs:323-326)
  use stride 0. An `out` may carry ANY stride on a length-1 dim (`check_out_buf_impl` ignores them):
  any op that multiplies such a stride (`l * out_strides[k]`, `n * out_strides[k]`, `stride*step`)
  must only do so for a dim it actually steps (repeat.rs:173-177 and slice.rs:163-169 special-case).
- 0-stride inputs (Scalar pull: one item, all-0 strides, storage/scalar.rs:98-103; Broadcast pull):
  Flip/Repeat/Tile read through them; Slice keeps them 0.
- NDIM_MAX=8: InsertDim/Stack/Reshape/SliceSpec check; Repeat/Tile need ndim <= 7. RemoveDim
  validates while iterating (remove_dim.rs:57-75).
- Struct dtypes / inner shapes / itemsize != alignment: ops treat an element as `itemsize` opaque bytes;
  NdCopier picks a typed copy by (itemsize, alignment) (util/nd_copy.rs:28-39). Join ops compare full
  `Dtype`.
- 32-bit: request sizes are bounded, dims are not. Ops that turn a DIM-scale u64 into usize: Slice box
  size (slice.rs:157-159), `step as usize` (160, 169). Tile case C reads the full period `l as usize`
  (tile.rs:198) only when `total > l`, so it is bounded.
- Boundary-straddling reads: Concatenate pieces (borders, zero-length members anywhere), Roll wrap
  (`s < shift < e`, roll.rs:106), Tile period (`s_in + total` vs `l`), Repeat head/middle/tail
  (repeat.rs:205-229), Slice steps not dividing the length (`div_ceil`, slice.rs:425-429).

## Intentional behaviors
- Slice: step >= 1 only (slice.rs:414-419, test `error_negative_step`). Bounds are strict: out-of-range
  or start > end is an error, not clamped; start == end and start == dim_len are accepted
  (slice.rs:387-412, tests `resolve_rejects_*` / `resolve_accepts_*`). Rust ranges -> SliceItem
  (slice.rs:332-353): `..=-1` means "to the end", bounds convert with saturating `i64::try_from`, the
  `+ 1` of an inclusive end saturates (K68, #91). Python allows only step 1
  (jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:335-336).
- Known slow paths, not bugs: Reshape reads split/merge reshapes one element at a time (K69: the
  read-time scan at reshape.rs:278-296 lets an unmatched new dim consume all remaining orig dims, so
  `[N]->[1,N]`, `[6,4]->[2,3,4]` match nothing despite the comment at 191-197); stepped Slice over a
  non-plain inner reads one position at a time (K77, slice.rs:174-210).
- Broadcast requires equal ndim (broadcast.rs:9-9); Python prepends dims via InsertDim and accepts
  `-1` (jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:56-128).
- Tile never adds leading dims, unlike numpy (tile.rs:11-11, 339-340). Repeat takes one scalar count.
  Both reject ndim == NDIM_MAX (tests `error_ndim_equals_ndim_max`).
- InsertDim uses numpy `expand_dims` output positions, duplicates rejected (insert_dim.rs:10-10).
  RemoveDim: only length-1 dims, duplicates rejected. Flip: empty dim list and dims of length <= 1
  are no-ops (flip.rs:8-8, 59-61; tests `identity_*`). Roll: one dim, shift reduced modulo length,
  length 0 means shift 0 (roll.rs:50-55).
- Reshape takes `&[u64]` (no `-1`; Python resolves it, jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:716-770) and is
  documented to read-amplify (reshape.rs:10-11).
- Rust Concatenate/Stack require identical dtypes (concatenate.rs:25-25, stack.rs:25); Python promotes
  first and requires equal ndim; Python `concatenate` of one array returns it unchanged and `stack` of
  one array becomes InsertDim (jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:872-876, 984-988).
- Flip, Repeat, Reshape, Stack, Roll(wrap), Tile(B/C), Concatenate(across members) materialize in pull
  mode; strides are usize so Flip cannot be a view. Broadcast push always copies.
- Block shape, fixed dims, scale weights and cache ids are performance hints; a wrong value is not a
  correctness bug (the layout order is the exception, see Contracts).

## Hot spots
Marked [new] = new or changed since 6dbeb15 (git diff -M 6dbeb15 HEAD). Churn: #94 (ArrayParams),
#95 e6ef7ee (identity fast paths, Concatenate forward, Flip skip), #97/#98 (file moves), #100 2d5e279
(cache scopes), #103 c28c62a (`Index`), #104 7ebac4c (`OutBuf`/slot).
- [RULED OUT in batch7-6 for 64-bit: every derived size is non-zero (audited by concept-degenerate-shapes and concept-composition, plus a 40k-case shape-op differential); 32-bit Slice is K156] [new] Index/OutBuf migration in every `read_data`: with the empty-read returns gone, can any op
  still build a zero size via `new_unchecked` (release has no check; zero `NonZeroUsize` is UB)?
  Check derived sizes: slice.rs:157-159 box, roll.rs:116-117, tile.rs:162-163, 197,
  repeat.rs:129-135, concatenate.rs:290-296.
- [new] Slot plumbing: `read_data_pull_in(.., slot)` writes into the caller's slot and the op then
  relabels it (buf.rs:540-546, slice.rs:161-170, broadcast.rs:157-162). `write_out_buf_slot` asserts
  an empty slot (buf.rs:503-515). Does any path pull twice into one slot, or materialize after the
  slot was filled?
- [new] Identity fast paths (e6ef7ee): Slice/Flip/Roll forward spec + `as_compact()` when identity.
  Is `is_identity` exactly "same values, same shape" (Slice: steps 1 and full length => start 0;
  Flip: only length <= 1 dims; Roll: shift 0)? `write_to` emits the inner's blocks under the outer
  shape. Flip/Roll identity skip `check_out_buf` and their cache scope; Slice identity still enters
  its scope while advertising the inner's cache ids (perf only, since hits need exact indices).
- [new] Concatenate forward (concatenate.rs:218-243): `first_arr` (linear for <= 32 borders,
  `partition_point` otherwise) skips zero-length members; the member gets `req_start - arr_start` and
  the caller's `out` (push or pull). Any request on a border, or after trailing empty members?
- [new] Cache scopes (2d5e279): every op except Broadcast and front-InsertDim. Values cannot change
  (exact-index hits), but check scope guards are dropped in order and that a cached `Shared` pull
  buffer escaping a scope is never written (it is read-only; `Arc::into_inner` in buf_pool.rs:59-63).
- Push-mode offsets in split ops: does each inner read land at `out + sum(offset_d * stride_d)` and do
  the pieces tile the region exactly once, for permuted / padded / length-1-dim-stride `out`, and for
  the sub-buffers `to_buf_strided_slow_dyn` passes (array/read.rs:509-557)?
- Reshape read (reshape.rs:278-369) vs constructor scan (61-73: no advance on match, no length check,
  so two new dims can map to one orig dim; only `one_to_one` (106-130) guards the layout order). The
  `flat` decomposition (350-354) omits matched dims; it is right only because matched dims are a
  prefix with equal lengths and skipped orig dims before them have length 1. Any change to the scan
  (e.g. fixing K69) must revisit `flat` and `orig_strides`.
- Repeat `copy_region` (repeat.rs:147-203): (ndim+1)-d split with stride `n * out_strides[k]` and 0
  source stride; `first_out_k - s`, `p_end_tail`, and `g_count == 1` vs head/middle/tail.
- Tile cases (tile.rs:148-292): boundaries `s_in + total <= l` / `total <= l`, case C extents, the
  synthesized stride-0 dim at k with dst stride `l * out_strides[k]` (253).
- Flip (flip.rs:105-165): mirrored inner start `L - e`, `dst_off = (len-1-idx)*stride` over several
  flipped dims; src offsets on a 0-stride inner.
- Stack `in_place` uses the ARRAY shape before `stack_dim` (stack.rs:203-204) while Concatenate's
  `inner_contiguous` uses the REQUEST shape (concatenate.rs:257-262); both need a packed `out`.
- Spec propagation: InsertDim splice (insert_dim.rs:87-114), RemoveDim `out_dim` (101-113), Stack
  shift+insert (stack.rs:125-131), Reshape `one_to_one`, Concatenate `max_cost_layout_order`.

### Suspicions (unverified)
- [CONFIRMED in batch7-1 as K159] flip.rs:53-61 - [new] the `size <= 1` skip runs before `is_flipped[d] = true`, so a repeated dim of
  length <= 1 passes the duplicate check: `flip([0, 0])` on shape [1, 4] returns Ok, though the docs
  (flip.rs:225) and test `error_duplicate_dim` promise duplicates are rejected.
- [CONFIRMED in batch7-1 as K156] slice.rs:157-159 - 32-bit: the pull fast-path box size `(n - 1) * step as usize + 1` is usize math;
  a PLAIN_READ inner whose dim exceeds usize::MAX (Scalar shapes need only fit u64,
  storage/scalar.rs:44-58; also InsertDim/RemoveDim/identity views of it) overflows, e.g. u8 Scalar
  [2^33], step 2^32-1, read [0..2]: debug panic; release wraps to box size 0, an Index built by
  `new_unchecked` with a zero `NonZeroUsize` (UB), though the values happen to stay right.

## Review units
Line counts exclude the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the bottom of each file (use those tests freely).

shape-ops-forwarders (~1120 lines): permute_dims.rs:1-203, insert_dim.rs:1-247, remove_dim.rs:1-241,
broadcast.rs:1-221, storage/buf.rs:351-554. Consult storage/index.rs, storage/core_trait.rs,
storage/params.rs, context.rs:118-290, storage/plain.rs, storage/scalar.rs.
- [new] `read_data_and_map_strides` relabels the caller's slot in place (buf.rs:540-546): can the
  relabel ever give a WRITABLE inner buffer aliasing strides (0 only on extent-1 dims)?
- Are the two stride closures exact inverses for unsorted, adjacent, leading/trailing inserted or
  removed dims, and is the push-mode `out` the callee sees still extent-correct?
- [new] Cache scopes: Broadcast never scopes and InsertDim skips it for front insertions
  (insert_dim.rs:123-127); does anything depend on a scope for values, or leak/hold a cache map?
- Broadcast: pull makes the buffer read-only before 0 strides; push copies from a pull of
  `[0..1]` broadcast dims. Any path that writes through or forwards a 0-stride buffer?
- `check_out_buf_impl` (buf.rs:383-431): sorted-stride disjointness and extent for padded,
  permuted, and length-1-dim-stride outs; is any overlapping or short `out` accepted?
- Spec: layout-order permutation validity (InsertDim splice, RemoveDim renumbering, PermuteDims
  `inv_dims`) and per-dim array lengths; flags kept (PLAIN_READ) vs cleared.

shape-ops-slice-reshape (~880 lines): slice.rs:1-450, reshape.rs:1-426. Consult storage/buf.rs,
storage/index.rs, storage/params.rs, util/mod.rs, error.rs:192-312, archive/array.rs:397-416,
jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:294-389.
- [new] Identity Slice forwards spec, IS_COMPACT and `as_compact()` (slice.rs:120-122, 223-241):
  is `is_identity` exactly "start 0, step 1, full length"? Is `write_to` then correct?
- [new] Plain pull fast path rewritten on the slot (slice.rs:149-172): box start/size, stride*step vs
  itemsize for length-1 dims, 32-bit usize overflow of the box size (see Suspicions).
- General stepped path (178-212): per-item sub-buffer offsets with permuted/padded/push `out`;
  `inner_size` for step-1 dims; every element written once?
- `DimSlice::resolve` and the range conversions (slice.rs:332-429): negative, inclusive, saturated,
  start == len, zero-length dims.
- Reshape read: matched-prefix invariant, `flat` decomposition, `orig_strides` (dummy 0 on
  unmatched orig dims) and `read_size` for 0-d, length-1 and trailing-1 shapes.
- Reshape::new: `try_shape_product().unwrap()` on the inner shape (50), constructor scan mapping two
  new dims to one orig dim, `one_to_one` layout order.

shape-ops-copy-ops (~1080 lines): flip.rs:1-231, roll.rs:1-209, repeat.rs:1-286, tile.rs:1-349.
Consult storage/buf.rs, storage/index.rs, util/nd_copy.rs, util/mod.rs:621-629, array/read.rs:450-557.
- [new] Flip size<=1 skip (flip.rs:58-60) vs duplicate check, and the identity path that bypasses
  `check_out_buf` and the cache scope (94-96); identity spec/`as_compact()`.
- [new] Roll identity (shift 0) and non-wrap forwarding of `out` (roll.rs:106-111): `j_start` when
  `e <= shift`; wrap split lengths and dst offsets.
- Every `get_unchecked(_mut)` offset: provably <= slice length for all requests, incl. 0-stride
  inner dims and length-1 out dims with huge strides?
- Repeat head/middle/tail cover each output position exactly once for every `s mod n`, `e mod n`;
  (ndim+1)-d shapes and strides; stride special case for `g_len <= 1`.
- Tile case A/B/C boundaries, case C head/middle/tail extents vs `out_shape`, stride-0 synthesized

- Sub-Index sizes (roll len1/len2, tile len1/len2/l, repeat g_count) are never 0 or truncated.

shape-ops-join (~830 lines): concatenate.rs:1-349, stack.rs:1-270, util/arr_sequence.rs:53-197,
util/arr_sequence.rs:592-655. Consult storage/buf.rs, storage/params.rs:852-1001,
